Platform Architecture

One integration. The entire logistics stack.

Connect your store or ERP once. SwiftShip and WareSync work in concert — purchase orders trigger GRN workflows in WareSync, fulfilled orders route to the best carrier via SwiftShip, and every event flows back to your system via webhooks.

01

Order ingestion & routing

Orders sync from Shopify, Amazon, Meesho or your ERP. SwiftShip scores carriers on rate, speed, and performance history.

02

WMS-driven fulfillment

WareSync generates pick lists, guides put-away staff, and manages multi-node inventory in real time.

03

Last-mile dispatch & tracking

Shipments dispatch via the optimal carrier. Branded tracking page updates in real time. NDR triggers auto-retry logic.

04

COD reconciliation & analytics

COD remittances reconcile automatically. SLA dashboards surface exceptions before they escalate.

Features

Everything your shipping team needs — in one platform

From carrier allocation to COD remittance, SwiftShip handles the full post-purchase workflow.

Smart Carrier Allocation

Auto-assign shipments to the best carrier based on zone, weight, COD amount, SLA, and performance history.

Multi-Carrier Rate Shopping

Compare live rates across 15+ carriers in under 100ms. Apply business rules to balance cost and speed.

Real-Time Tracking

Unified tracking events from every carrier. Push notifications via SMS, WhatsApp, and email.

NDR & RTO Management

Automated NDR escalation workflows. Customer re-engagement via WhatsApp. RTO reduction playbooks.

COD Reconciliation

Automatic matching of COD remittances from 15+ carriers. Exception flags and settlement reports.

SLA & Performance Dashboards

Carrier-level SLA scorecards, zone-wise performance heatmaps, and delay root-cause analysis.

100+ Integrations

Native connectors for Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, and all major ERPs.

REST API & Webhooks

Full-featured REST API with 99.9% uptime SLA. Real-time webhooks for every shipment event.

Returns Management

Initiate return pickups from SwiftShip. Auto-generate reverse AWBs. QC integration with WareSync.

Ship smarter. Reduce RTO. Reconcile faster.

Most customers see 15–20% freight cost reduction in the first 60 days.

WMS Features

Purpose-built for high-throughput fulfilment

From GRN to dispatch — every warehouse workflow digitised and optimised.

Inbound & GRN

Barcode/QR scanning for goods receipt. Automated PO matching, discrepancy alerts, and vendor scorecards.

Put-Away & Slotting

Intelligent slotting based on velocity, weight, and pick frequency. Directed put-away to handheld devices.

Multi-Node Inventory

Real-time inventory visibility across all your warehouses, dark stores, and retail outlets.

Pick-Pack-Ship

Wave, zone, and cluster picking. Packing station integration with weight validation.

Cycle Counts & Audits

Scheduled and on-demand cycle counts. Variance reports with root-cause tagging.

Returns & Reverse Logistics

Receive, grade, and reroute returned items. QC disposition workflows: restock, refurbish, liquidate.

ERP & OMS Integration

Native sync with SAP, Oracle, Tally, and major OMS platforms. Bi-directional inventory updates.

Multi-Client / Multi-Tenant

Run multiple brand or client operations from one WareSync instance. Separate P&L and inventory isolation.

Ops Dashboards

Throughput, dwell time, picker productivity, and SLA adherence — live on mobile or wall screen.

Cut mis-ships. Accelerate dispatch. Scale without chaos.

WareSync customers typically cut order processing time by 40% within 90 days of go-live.

Freight Services

Intercity freight, tracked and SLA-backed

Full Truckload (FTL)

Dedicated trucks from 9ft to 40ft trailers. Tata, Ashok Leyland, and Eicher fleet. Transit time commitments.

Part Truckload (PTL)

Load consolidation for shipments under 2,000 kg. Shared lanes reduce your per-kg cost by 30–50% vs FTL.

GPS Tracking

Real-time vehicle location on every FTL movement. ETA updates every 30 minutes.

800+ Lanes

Established lanes across the golden quadrilateral and all major production-to-distribution corridors.

Digital Documentation

E-way bill generation, e-POD, digital LR, and GSTIN invoice — all managed in our freight portal.

Factory & Hub Pickups

Scheduled factory pickups with dock-slot booking. Integration with WareSync for seamless inbound.

1. About This Policy

This Privacy Policy is published by SendIt Logistics Private Limited (CIN: U74999KA2025PTC123456), a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, with its registered office at BHIVE Platinum, 48, Church Street, Ashok Nagar, Bengaluru – 560 001, Karnataka, India ("SendIt", "we", "us", or "our").

SendIt operates the SwiftShip courier orchestration platform, the WareSync warehouse management system, and provides third-party logistics (3PL) services. This Policy is framed in compliance with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDPA 2023").

2. Data We Collect

2.1 Account and Business Data

When you register for SwiftShip or WareSync, we collect your name, business name, GST number, work email address, mobile number, billing address, and payment instrument details (stored via our PCI-DSS-compliant payment processor).

2.2 Shipment and Consignee Data

In the course of processing shipments, we collect and process the following data about end consignees: full name, delivery address (including PIN code), mobile number or email address for delivery notifications, order value (for COD purposes), and package contents description.

2.3 Rider and Fleet Location Data

For last-mile delivery operations, we collect real-time GPS location data from our rider application. This data is used solely for route optimisation, live tracking provision, COD accountability, and operational performance monitoring.

3. How We Use Your Data

We use personal data for: providing and operating the platforms; fulfilling 3PL service obligations; processing payments and COD reconciliation; sending shipment tracking notifications; conducting security monitoring; complying with applicable law; and improving our services through aggregate analytics.

4. Third-Party Sharing

We share personal data with: carrier partners (shipment data for delivery purposes); payment processors (Razorpay, Cashfree); cloud infrastructure providers (AWS Mumbai region); communication service providers (SMS/WhatsApp notifications); and regulatory authorities when required by applicable Indian law. We do not sell personal data to any third party.

5. Data Retention

Shipment and consignee data is retained for 7 years from the date of shipment. Account data is retained for the duration of the customer relationship and for 7 years thereafter. Rider location data is retained in raw form for 90 days and in aggregated form for 3 years.

6. Your Rights Under DPDPA 2023

You have the right to access, correction, erasure, and grievance redressal in respect of your personal data. To exercise any of these rights, contact our DPO at sales@sendit.co.in. We will respond within 30 days.

7. Cookies

Our website uses strictly necessary cookies (session management, security) and analytics cookies (Google Analytics 4, deployed only with consent). Advertising and tracking cookies are not deployed on our Platforms.

8. Security

We implement industry-standard security controls including TLS 1.2+ encryption in transit, AES-256 encryption at rest, role-based access controls, and multi-factor authentication.

Operations

How to reduce RTO by 30% in 60 days

SendIt Team·Aug 2026·6 min read

Non-delivery reports (NDRs) are the single biggest margin killer in Indian e-commerce. The average D2C brand loses 18-25% of shipments to RTO. At Rs 80-120 per returned shipment, that adds up fast.

18-25%
Avg D2C RTO rate
Rs 100+
Cost per return
30%
Reduction in 60 days

Why RTO happens

Our analysis of 800,000+ shipments shows five root causes account for 90% of all returns:

  • Wrong or incomplete address (34%)
  • Customer unavailability - repeated attempts failed (28%)
  • Customer refused delivery - usually COD (19%)
  • Carrier could not locate the address (11%)
  • Shipment damaged in transit (8%)

Step 1-4: Address hygiene

Before a shipment leaves your warehouse, run every order through:

  • PIN code validation against serviceable areas
  • Address standardisation
  • Duplicate order detection
  • Mobile number format validation
SwiftShip runs address validation at order ingestion. Brands using this see a 40% drop in address-not-found NDRs.

Step 5-8: Carrier allocation

Not all carriers perform equally in every zone. Allocating blindly by rate causes unnecessary RTO.

  • Score carriers by zone-level delivery rate, not just cost
  • Avoid low-performing carriers in Tier 3 zones even if cheaper
  • Split COD and prepaid orders - COD needs higher-reliability carriers
  • Track carrier NDR patterns and auto-blacklist underperformers
SwiftShip's allocation engine scores carriers on 14 signals including zone performance, COD remittance speed, and last-mile network density.

Step 9-12: NDR re-engagement

When a delivery fails, the next 24 hours are critical.

  • Auto-trigger WhatsApp message within 2 hours of NDR event
  • Let customers reschedule via a link - no call centre needed
  • Offer alternate pickup point for Tier 1 cities
  • After 3 failed attempts, auto-cancel COD and convert to return

Brands that deploy WhatsApp NDR re-engagement see 60-70% of NDR shipments successfully delivered on retry.

WMS

Cycle count vs full stock audit

SendIt Team·Jul 2026·5 min read

Most warehouse managers default to the full stock audit - shut everything down for 2 days, count every SKU, reconcile. It is disruptive, expensive, and by the time you fix the variance, new errors have already crept in.

Cycle counting is the alternative: count a rotating subset of inventory continuously, so every SKU gets counted 3-4 times per year without stopping operations.

Why full audits fail at scale

For warehouses with 500+ SKUs, annual full audits have a fundamental problem: the count is stale the moment it is done.

  • Full audit takes 16-48 hours of downtime
  • Reconciliation takes another 2-3 days
  • Error rate during manual counting: 3-5% on average
  • By the time you act on the data, it is already outdated
One FMCG brand on WareSync found Rs 4.8L in phantom inventory through cycle counting - stock that appeared in the system but had not physically existed for months.

How cycle counting works

Divide your inventory into zones or ABC categories:

  • A-class SKUs (top 20% by value/velocity) - count weekly
  • B-class SKUs - count monthly
  • C-class SKUs - count quarterly
  • Trigger-based counts after any unusual movement

Getting started in 3 steps

  • Classify your SKUs into A/B/C by sales velocity
  • Set count frequency and variance tolerance per class
  • Run the WareSync cycle count task generator - it does the scheduling automatically

COD reconciliation: why numbers never match

SendIt Team·Jun 2026·5 min read

If you are processing more than 500 COD orders a month, you have probably experienced this: the amount deposited by your carrier does not match your expected remittance. This is a structural problem with how COD reconciliation works.

The 5 root causes

  • Remittance cycle mismatch: carriers remit on different cycles (T+2 to T+10), orders from different periods get mixed
  • Short shipments excluded: carriers deduct undelivered COD without always notifying you
  • Weight dispute deductions: overweight charges auto-deducted from COD pool
  • Bank charges: some carriers deduct NEFT/RTGS charges from remittance
  • Exchange/return deductions: reverse logistics charges deducted inline

How SwiftShip handles it

  • Pulls remittance files from all carriers via API daily
  • Matches each remittance line to an AWB and order
  • Flags unmatched remittances and short payments automatically
  • Generates a dispute file pre-formatted for each carrier portal
Brands using SwiftShip COD reconciliation recover an average of Rs 80,000-1,20,000 per month in previously undetected short payments.

What to do right now

  • Download last 3 months of remittance data from all your carriers
  • Map each remittance line to an AWB in your OMS
  • Calculate expected vs actual for each carrier
  • Flag discrepancies above Rs 50 per shipment for dispute

FTL/PTL

FTL vs PTL: a guide for FMCG distribution

SendIt Team·May 2026·6 min read

FMCG brands moving goods from factory to distributor or warehouse face a recurring decision: book a full truck or consolidate loads? The wrong choice adds 15-40% to your per-kg freight cost.

FTL: when it makes sense

Full Truckload (FTL) is right when:

  • Your shipment fills 70%+ of a truck (typically 5-10 tonnes+)
  • Transit time is critical - FTL is point-to-point, no stops
  • You are moving high-value or fragile goods
  • The lane runs daily or multiple times per week

Typical FTL rates in India (2026): Rs 18-32 per tonne-km on major lanes.

PTL: when it makes sense

Part Truckload (PTL) is right when:

  • Shipment is under 3-4 tonnes
  • Frequency is low (once or twice a week per lane)
  • Destination is served by a consolidation hub
  • Cost per kg matters more than transit time
SendIt's PTL network covers 120+ lanes with consolidation hubs in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Hyderabad, and Chennai.

The hybrid strategy

Most FMCG brands with national distribution use a hybrid:

  • FTL for factory-to-warehouse (high volume, regular)
  • PTL for warehouse-to-distributor (variable volume, multiple destinations)
  • Express courier for urgent replenishment of fast-moving SKUs

Why your per-order logistics cost is too high

SendIt Team·May 2026·7 min read

Most D2C founders can quote their customer acquisition cost to two decimal places. Ask them their per-order fulfilment cost and you will get a shrug. This is one of the biggest reasons D2C margins look worse than they should.

The full cost formula

True per-order logistics cost = Storage cost + Pick and pack + Outbound delivery + Returns cost (weighted by RTO rate) + COD fee (weighted by COD mix)

Most brands calculate only the outbound delivery charge and ignore the rest. This understates true logistics cost by 35-60%.
Rs 28-45
Outbound delivery (prepaid, 500g, Tier 1)
Rs 12-20
Pick and pack labour
Rs 8-15
Storage per order
Rs 18-35
RTO cost at 20% RTO rate

Benchmarks by order value

  • Order value under Rs 500: logistics should be under 18% of order value
  • Order value Rs 500-1,500: logistics should be under 12%
  • Order value above Rs 1,500: logistics should be under 8%
  • If you are above these: high RTO, expensive packaging, or under-negotiating carrier rates

The biggest levers

  • Reduce RTO rate by 5% - saves Rs 8-12 per order at average volumes
  • Shift 20% of COD orders to prepaid - saves Rs 15-25 per converted order
  • Negotiate weight slabs - most brands pay 500g slab for 200g products
  • Move to a 3PL closer to your customer concentration zone

Cookie Policy

Contents
1. What are cookies2. Cookies we use3. Third-party cookies4. Managing cookies5. Contact
Last updated: 5 August 2026

1. What Are Cookies

Cookies are small text files placed on your device when you visit a website. They allow the website to recognise your device on subsequent visits, remember your preferences, and provide a personalised experience.

2. Cookies We Use

2.1 Strictly Necessary Cookies

These cookies are essential for the operation of our website and platforms. You cannot opt out of strictly necessary cookies.

  • session_id — Maintains your login session. Duration: session.
  • csrf_token — Protects against cross-site request forgery. Duration: session.
  • cookie_consent — Stores your cookie preference. Duration: 12 months.

2.2 Analytics Cookies

We use Google Analytics 4. These cookies collect information in aggregate form and only placed with your consent.

  • _ga — Distinguishes users. Duration: 2 years.
  • _ga_* — Session state. Duration: 2 years.

2.3 Functional Cookies

These cookies enable enhanced functionality such as remembering your language preference or region.

2.4 Marketing & Advertising Cookies

We currently do not deploy advertising cookies or tracking pixels on our website. If this changes, we will update this policy and seek fresh consent.

3. Third-Party Cookies

Certain features involve third-party services that may set their own cookies:

  • Google Analytics — Website analytics
  • Intercom — Customer support chat widget
  • Google Fonts — Typography rendering

4. Managing Cookies

You can control and manage cookies in several ways:

  • Browser settings: Most browsers allow you to refuse or delete cookies.
  • Opt-out tools: Google Analytics opt-out at tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout
  • Cookie banner: Choose which categories to accept via our consent banner on first visit.

5. Contact

Questions about cookies? Contact our DPO at sales@sendit.co.in
